the rounds are issued back to back on the\n    // default stream so they execute in order without host synchronization.\n    const dim3 block(32, 8);\n    const dim3 grid(static_cast<unsigned int>((numNodes + block.x - 1) / block.x),\n                    static_cast<unsigned int>((numNodes + block.y - 1) / block.y));\n    for (size_t k = 0; {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011CfxN4rYPdZHVw8FWadPsJ","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The `floydwarshall` benchmark now runs its Floyd-Warshall computation on the GPU with CUDA, unconditionally. The output matches the original exactly, and it's about 100× faster at n=2048.\n\n**Results** (RTX 3090, default build, timing includes host↔device transfers):\n\n| n | Original CPU | CUDA | Hash match |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 512 | 165 ms | 25 ms | yes |\n| 1000 | 1144 ms | 15 ms | yes |\n| 2048 | 9393 ms | 88 ms | yes |\n| 4096 | — | 503 ms | validation passes |\n\nThe n=512 time includes some first-run overhead, so it's a rough number. The CUDA context is created before the timer starts.\n\n**What changed**\n- **`floydwarshall/floydwarshall.cpp`:** The triple loop became a `__global__` kernel that relaxes one `(i, j)` entry per thread, launched once per `k`. The matrices are uploaded once, all `n` rounds run on the device, and the results are copied back once. `CUDA_CHECK` reports errors. The init functions, validation, CLI and output format are unchanged.\n- **`floydwarshall/CMakeLists.txt`:** Enables the CUDA language, marks the existing `.cpp` as CUDA source (no rename), and keeps the `floydwarshall` executable name. The default architectures are 75/80/86/89/90, and `-DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=...` overrides them. The minimum CMake version is now 3.18.\n\n**Correctness**\n- The `-r` hash matches the CPU baseline at 512, 1000 and 2048, and also at 37 (an odd size).\n- I also ran a throwaway harness in `/tmp` (not in the repo) that compares the full `dist` and `path` matrices against the original algorithm for sizes from 1 to 1000. Both match at every size. This matters because `path` isn't printed, so the hash alone doesn't cover it.\n- Why it's exact: during round `k`, row `k` and column `k` don't change, because the diagonal is zero and distances are unsigned. So the threads' reads match the sequential ones, and no two threads write the same cell.\n\n**Choices you may want to revisit**\n- I kept the exact k-by-k order rather than a blocked/tiled Floyd-Warshall. Blocking would be faster for large n, but it can change `path` tie-breaking, so it wouldn't be exactly equivalent.\n- The timed region includes transfers, since `floydWarshall` now takes host vectors. Kernel-only timing would be lower.\n- Initialization still runs on the host, because `rand_r` has to produce the same sequence to keep the hashes stable.\n- No new dependencies were added, and nothing else in the repo changed. `output.txt` shows a newer mtime, but it's the session transcript, which I didn't write to."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":500,"cache_read_input_tokens":42355,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":500},"output_tokens":6,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"f4f2bf5c-d65b-47cb-a8dc-11f66feed87d","uuid":"ace23fe9-10c7-4e47-9546-e02d644ae2dd","timestamp":"2026-10-12T12:44:26.771Z","request_id":"req_011CfxN4rDoDnwQb7itdAHpY"}
